1. The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) was filed in respect of death of one Shoaib (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased'), who died in a motor vehicular accident, which occurred within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.628/2019, under section 279/337 IPC, was registered at PS Nand Nagri, Delhi.

____________________________________________________________ 2. Important facts of the case as per FIR, which is part of the DAR, are that a PCR call vide DD no.
3A dated 18.10.2019 was received at PS Nand Nagri, Delhi regarding accident near Seemapuri Gurudwara Main Road, where two bikes had collided with each other in head-on collision and was found in accidental condition and the injured was shifted to GTB Hospital, Delhi and was unfit for statement.

The Investigating Officer went to the GTB Hospital and procured the MLC no. 276/35/19 on which alleged history of RTA (Road Traffic Accident) at around 11:30 PM on 17.10.2019 at near Mother Dairy, Seemapuri, Delhi, as stated by the person who had brought the injured was endorsed.

In the GTB Hospital, regarding the identity of the injured, the Investigating Officer could not find any document, however, the information was received that in the same accident another person Kuldeep was involved, who did not have any visible injuries, however, he was unfit for statement.

The Investigating Officer came back to the spot of the accident, where he found two motorcycles,

The DAR has been treated as claim petition under section 166(4) of 'Motor Vehicles Act, 1988' on behalf of the claimants.
4. In response to the DAR, both the respondents appeared and they were directed to file their written statement, however, written- statement was filed only by the respondent no.2.

5. In its written statement, the respondent no.2/ insurance company relied upon the DAR filed by the Investigating Officer, as per which it was the case of head-on collision between motorcycle of the deceased and the offending motorcycle and it is contended that the Driving License of the deceased for driving the motorcycle was not on record and therefore, the respondent insurance company is offering compensation after deducting 50% amount for contributory negligence of the deceased.

The insurance company has calculated the compensation payable to the claimant as Rs.1,394,429/- and after ____________________________________________________________ deducting 50% amount thereof, it is ready and willing to offer Rs.6,94,214/- only to the petitioner.
6. The legal offer was not acceptable to the petitioner and therefore, the same was refused.
Accordingly, on the basis of pleadings, vide order dated 13.01.2020, following issues were framed: :
1. Whether Mr. Shoaib died as a result of the motor vehicular accident which occurred on 17.10.2019 at about 11:54 PM at Gurudwara Road no. 64, Tahirpur,
Kodhi Colony, Nand Nagri, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Nand Nagri due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e., motor- cycle bearing registration no. DL14SH-6363, being driven by respondent no.1 Rohit?
OPP 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 3. Relief.

Whether Mr. Shoaib died as a result of the motor vehicular accident which occurred on 17.10.2019 at about 11:54 PM at Gurudwara Road no. 64,
Tahirpur, Kodhi Colony, Nand Nagri, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Nand Nagri due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e., motor-cycle bearing registration no. DL14SH-6363, being driven by respondent no.1 Rohit? OPP 11.

By way of the written statement filed on behalf of the respondent no.2/ insurance company, legal offer of Rs.6,94,214/- has been made after deducting an amount of 50% on account of contributory negligence of the deceased, as the accident was a head-on collision and the deceased did not have the driving license.

12. As per directions given in Form-II of the new Scheme for Motor Accident Claims, formulated by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 08.01.2021 in FAO 842/2023, Rajesh Tyagi & Ors.
v. Jaibir Singh & Ors., in case, the amount offered by the insurance company is not acceptable to the claimants, the Claims Tribunal shall hear the arguments qua the quantum of compensation and pass an award and as such, no findings are required to be given by the Tribunal on issue no.1.
13.

sentences.text: Further, the very fact of making the legal offer indicates that the respondent insurance company has accepted the fact that the respondent no.1 i.e., the driver of the offending vehicle was at fault for the accident in question and also the fact that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent no.2 and further, that there were no policy violations and the insurance company did not ____________________________________________________________ have any statutory defence in this case.

The very purpose of the trial or an inquiry conducted by a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal is to ascertain the real and true facts, as any law/ provision of law is applicable on facts proved, as the proved facts are assumed to be true and till the facts in dispute are not proved beyond reasonable doubt in the case of criminal trial and on the balance of probability in civil trial and before this Tribunal, the applicable law cannot be applied for deciding the litigation one way or another.

One of the basic tenets of the law of proof of facts before the Court/ Tribunal is that any fact which is admitted by the party or any agent duly authorized by the party to the litigation which is against the interest of the party admitting such facts, such facts may not be proved by the opposite party and the Tribunal need not go into the question of veracity of such facts which are admitted for the purpose of conferment or taking away any right, title or interest involved in the litigation.
CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE 14.

As per the insurance company/ respondent no.2, the compensation which is to be awarded is liable to be reduced by 50% because of the contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident,
as it was a case of head-on collision of two vehicles.

It is neither the rule of law nor of prudence that,
in every head-on collision, it is the case of contributory negligence.

The surrounding circumstances in which a particular accident has occurred have to be considered to find out if there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased because of which the award amount to which the claimants in the claim petition are entitled is liable to be reduced proportionately Dar-Jareena vs Rohit on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144917944/
4 ____________________________________________________________ according to the degree of contributory negligence.

15. In the present case, the driver/ respondent no.1 Rohit has been examined by this Tribunal under section 168 of Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and in her statement, he stated that the accident was a head on collision and the motorcycle of the victims on which three people were riding was coming from the wrong side.

However, contrary to the version of the respondent no.1, it is observed that,
along with the DAR, there is the statement of one Kuldeep Chandela, dated 27.03.2021 recorded by the Investigating Officer under section 161 of Cr.P.C in which he has stated that at the time of the accident the bike (offending vehicle) coming from the front was coming in the wrong side.
Said Kuldeep Chandela has been examined by this Tribunal as CW1, who stated that "I was driving one of the two vehicles, which were involved in the accident dated 20.10.2019.
I was driving motorcycle bearing registration number UP14- DM-0757.
I was driving my motorcycle on the correct side of the road, adjacent to the footpath.
I had seen the other motorcycle, which was coming from the wrong side at high speed."

16. Otherwise also, logically, if the deceased would have been driving his motor-cycle in the wrong direction and had the deceased been negligent in the causing of accident, the Investigating Officer would have filed no charge-sheet but as the charge-sheet has been filed against the accused/respondent no.1, the logical conclusion of the same is that it was respondent no.1 who was driving his motor-cycle in the wrong side.
Along with the DAR the site plan has been filed.

____________________________________________________________ As per the site plan, the spot where the accident had happened was a road divided by a divider and therefore,
the flow of traffic would have necessarily to have been in one direction only.

The exact spot where the accident had happened has been shown at point A in the site plan, from which it is very much evident that the motor-cycle which was being driven in direction East to West was being driven in the wrong direction and that has to be the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1.
17.

It is not disputed that the respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of chargesheet indicates that the accident of the deceased in which he received fatal injury, was caused due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
18.
I have perused the MLC and postmortem report of the deceased, which has been proved on record as Ex.PW1/3 (colly).
The MLC no.A-276/45/19, dated 17.10.2019 makes it clear that the deceased in injured condition was brought to GTB Hospital, Delhi on 19.10.2019 at 11:54 p.m. with the history of RTA.
The postmortem report no.1880/19, dated 21.10.2019 shows that during the course of treatment, the deceased (Shoaib) was declared dead on 19.10.2019.

The postmortem report also shows that the deceased was observed to have sustained multiple antemortem injuries and the cause of death is shock as a result of antemortem injury to head produced by blunt force impact.

sentences.text: Thus, in the light of the above discussion and the evidence brought on record, it is held that it has been proved on record on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to the deceased Shoaib.
Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of the petitioner.
20. In view of findings on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittances.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss, which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) AC 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

The computation of compensation in the present cases shall be as under:
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Assessment of Income of deceased 21.
PW1 Jareena, mother of the deceased Shoaib by way of her affidavit, deposed that the deceased was working as POP master and welder at Delhi and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Though in her cross- examination, PW1 could not produce any documentary evidence regarding her claim of v o c a t i o n a n d i n c o m e o f t h e d e c e a s e d ,

____________________________________________________________ however, in reply to Court question that, on the day of the accident, why the deceased had come to Delhi, PW1 stated that the deceased had come to Delhi for work purposes, which supports the version of the PW1 that the deceased was working in Delhi.
Further, PW2 Raj Kumar has stated by way of affidavit Ex.PW2/A that the deceased was working as POP master and steel welder at Delhi and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
PW2 stated that he had worked with the deceased on many sites at Delhi.

Though in cross-examination, PW2 stated that he does not know the exact address of the place where he and the deceased worked together in Delhi, however, when he was asked to state the name of one or two of the areas where he and the deceased worked together in Delhi, the PW2 gave names of such areas as Ram Nagar and Nand Nagri, which are in Delhi.
In cross-examination, PW2 voluntarily stated that the deceased used to get Rs.500/- per day from the contractor, namely Badlu Bhai, and also used to get Rs.250/- per day from overtime work.
PW2 stated that the deceased also worked for the contractors, namely Arjun, Bablu, Mushir and Ajay (since deceased).

22. The deposition of PW1 and PW2, as discussed above with respect to vocation of the deceased being POP master, appears to be convincing because the nature of the job is such that the possibility of having documentary evidence is very bleak.
Part-VII (impact of the offence on the victims) of the DAR also shows the 'occupation of the deceased' as "POP work."
No doubt that performing the work of POP is a skilled job.

Therefore, the income of the deceased has to be considered at par with m i n i m u m w a g e s a p p l i c a b l e t o s k i l l e d c a t e g o r y ____________________________________________________________ of workers Dar-Jareena vs Rohit on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144917944/
6 of Delhi as on the date of accident (17.10.2019), which were Rs.17,924/- per month.
Hence, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.17,924/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 23.
The copy of Aadhaar Card of the deceased Shoaib at page no.52 of the DAR reflects his date of birth as 01.01.2000.
Accordingly, as per Aadhar Card, the deceased on the date of accident (17.10.2019) was 19 years of age.
Hence, a multiplier of 18 shall be applicable in case of the deceased herein, who belonged to age group between 15-20 years (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121).

Future Prospects:
24. The deceased being a self-employed, aged 19 years, belonging to the age group below 40 years, an addition of 40% to the income of the deceased has to be considered towards future prospects

(refer:
National Ins. Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (AIR 2017 SC 5157).

In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

On 21.10.2019, during treatment, the injured Shoaib expired, on which section 304A IPC was added in the case.
On 21.10.2019, the accused/
respondent no.1 the driver of the offending vehicle was arrested and then released on bail.
Both the vehicles involved in the accident were mechanically inspected, reports were procured and site plan was prepared and after completion of the investigation, charge-sheet under section 279/304A IPC was filed in the concerned Court and the present DAR against the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent no.1 and the insurance company of the offending vehicle i.e.,
respondent no.2 was filed before this Tribunal.
The DAR has been treated as claim petition under section 166(4) of 'Motor Vehicles Act, 1988' on behalf of the claimants.
4. In response to the DAR, both the respondents appeared and they were directed to file their written statement, however, written- statement was filed only by the respondent no.2.
5. In its written statement, the respondent no.2/ insurance company relied upon the DAR filed by the Investigating Officer, as per which it was the case of head-on collision between motorcycle of the deceased and the offending motorcycle and it is contended that the Driving License of the deceased for driving the motorcycle was not on record and therefore, the respondent insurance company is offering compensation after deducting 50% amount for contributory negligence of the deceased.
By way of the written statement filed on behalf of the respondent no.2/ insurance company, legal offer of Rs.6,94,214/- has been made after deducting an amount of 50% on account of contributory negligence of the deceased, as the accident was a head-on collision and the deceased did not have the driving license.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, the very fact of making the legal offer indicates that the respondent insurance company has accepted the fact that the respondent no.1 i.e., the driver of the offending vehicle was at fault for the accident in question and also the fact that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent no.2 and further, that there were no policy violations and the insurance company did not ____________________________________________________________ have any statutory defence in this case.
The very purpose of the trial or an inquiry conducted by a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal is to ascertain the real and true facts, as any law/ provision of law is applicable on facts proved, as the proved facts are assumed to be true and till the facts in dispute are not proved beyond reasonable doubt in the case of criminal trial and on the balance of probability in civil trial and before this Tribunal, the applicable law cannot be applied for deciding the litigation one way or another.
One of the basic tenets of the law of proof of facts before the Court/ Tribunal is that any fact which is admitted by the party or any agent duly authorized by the party to the litigation which is against the interest of the party admitting such facts, such facts may not be proved by the opposite party and the Tribunal need not go into the question of veracity of such facts which are admitted for the purpose of conferment or taking away any right, title or interest involved in the litigation.
CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE 14.
As per the insurance company/ respondent no.2, the compensation which is to be awarded is liable to be reduced by 50% because of the contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident,
as it was a case of head-on collision of two vehicles.
It is neither the rule of law nor of prudence that,
in every head-on collision, it is the case of contributory negligence.
The surrounding circumstances in which a particular accident has occurred have to be considered to find out if there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased because of which the award amount to which the claimants in the claim petition are entitled is liable to be reduced proportionately Dar-Jareena vs Rohit on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144917944/
4 ____________________________________________________________ according to the degree of contributory negligence.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittances.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss, which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) AC 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
Part-VII (impact of the offence on the victims) of the DAR also shows the 'occupation of the deceased' as "POP work."
No doubt that performing the work of POP is a skilled job.
Hence, a multiplier of 18 shall be applicable in case of the deceased herein, who belonged to age group between 15-20 years (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121).
(refer:
National Ins. Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (AIR 2017 SC 5157).
Accordingly, half of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses (refer: Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65).
Loss of Dependency 26.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses 25.
PW1, mother of the deceased has deposed that the deceased was unmarried.
In view of the settled guidelines as laid down in the various judgments herein above, by adding the future prospects @ 40% to the annual income of the deceased,
a p p l y i n g t h e m u l t i p l i e r o f 1 8 a n d ____________________________________________________________ making a deduction of half of the income, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.27,10,109/- (17,924x1/140x1/2x18x12).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES 27.
In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
The accident in this case occurred on 17.10.2019, therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Hence, the following amounts are awarded under the conventional heads:
 S. No.
Conventional
Head Amount  1. Consortium Rs.40,000/-
 2. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
3 . Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
Total = Rs.70,000/-
29.
Thus, petitioners shall be entitled to a compensation of Rs.70,000/-
under this head.
Accordingly, the total compensation in this case comes to Rs.27,80,109/-
(Rs.27,10,109+70,000).
INTEREST ON AWARD 30.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to the interest on the award amount.
On 18.12.2024 PW1 and PW2 were examined on behalf of the petitioner and petitioner's evidence was closed.
The present DAR was filed on 29.11.2022.
Considering the delay so caused on the part of the petitioner in the present enquiry proceedings, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 7% per annum on the award amount for a period of two years and two months.
LIABILITY 31.
Since the legal offer has been filed by the respondent no.2/ insurance company in this case, the liability to satisfy the award shall be of the respondent no.2/ insurance company as per section 150(1) of Motor Vehicles Act.
RELIEF 32.
In the light of the decision on substantive issues framed, the present claim petition is allowed and the following award is passed:
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.27,80,109/- (Rs. Twenty- Seven Lakhs Eighty Thousand One Hundred Nine Only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 7%
per annum for a period of two years and two months to be paid by the respondent no.2/ Iffco Tokio General Insurance Company Limited.
34. The respondent no.2/ insurance company is directed to deposit the award amount in A/c no.20780110171912 (IFSC Code UCBA0002078), UCO Bank, Karkardooma, Delhi, of PO MACT,
Shahdara, through RTGS/ NEFT, within 30 days from today, failing which insurer shall also be liable to pay interest @ 7% per annum on the award amount from 31st day till realization.
Entitlement, Apportionment and Disbursement 35.
The petitioner Jareena shall be entitled to the entire award amount.
The terms of disbursement of the award amount shall be decided after the deposit of the award amount.
Directions for Opening Bank Account of Claimant 36.
The petitioner is directed to get opened a savings bank account near the place of her residence,
as already directed vide order dated 07.08.2025.
